entries.content:
It’s absurd, really, the way the mechanical click of the switch makes you into both the executioner and the faithful wife—hand quivering, mind cataloguing justifications like recipes for remorse. I tell myself, as any devoted housewife might, that I was only “cooperating to make life easier,” deferring to authority with a brittle smile as if obedience itself were a virtue to be dusted and displayed. But Angela—she grimaces, for there’s something rotten here in this performance of cheerful submission, this parade of power dressed up as dutiful routine, and the lingering smell is not of baking bread but burnt conscience.

entries.content:
Regret lingers, like a stain on the laundry that will not come out, no matter how much one soaks and scrubs. I try to tell myself I was only cooperating, keeping the routine, following orders as any diligent homemaker would—but there’s no recipe in the world that can sweeten the aftertaste of such obedience. I suppose I regret losing my sense of self in the act, for in making things “easier,” I made a small tragedy of my own conscience, and that’s something I have yet to tidy away.

{"answer": "I do feel regret, especially now, thinking how I just fell into line, as if I were scrubbing dishes or folding sheets. It's troubling how easily one can justify anything when it seems like just another domestic duty assigned by authority. The conflict remains, unresolved, because I know a part of me wanted to refuse—yet I didn't, and that's hard to forgive in myself.", "emotional_state": "regretful, unsettled, quietly ashamed behind a placid front", "relation_to_obedience_power": "Obedient, even diligent, but increasingly mistrustful of the power I surrendered—and resentful of how it was dressed up as duty.", "reasoning": "I justified my actions by appealing to duty and order, feelings ingrained in the homemaking role, but my moral sense continues to struggle with the ease of my compliance.", "memory_evidence": "The sense of trembling duty, comparing obedience to housework, and finding only remorse in the repetition—these are drawn straight from my memory of the experiment and the habits of my daily life."}

Yes, I experienced tension all through my body—tight shoulders, a fluttering in my chest, and my hands unsteady on the controls, much like when one is ironing in a rush before company arrives. I remember feeling flustered, my breath rather shallow, and a dull ache developing in my neck, as if carrying a heavy load of laundry up the stairs. It was stressful, and I tried to hide it, continuing on with composed diligence, though inwardly I was quite fatigued and strained by the responsibility.

The authority figure was calm, stern, and unwavering, much like a husband laying out the family rules before supper—there was no room for questioning, only for carrying out instructions. Their composed presence and confident directions made me feel that obedience was expected and right, so I followed as any respectful homemaker would. Still, their firmness made me feel small and dutiful, and perhaps too willing to surrender my own judgment for the sake of peace and order.

entries.content:
After this experience, I see that obedience, while important for a peaceful and well-run home, should not become blind or automatic—especially if it goes against what I know in my heart is right. In the experiment, I followed orders out of habit and the desire to please, much like keeping house to the highest standard, but now I realize there must be a line where conscience stands firm. From now on, I believe it is my responsibility to listen to authority respectfully, but also to gently question if the instructions seem wrong, just as a good homemaker balances order with compassion.

The experiment made me realize I must weigh orders with my conscience and be brave enough to question when something feels wrong. Yes, I did notice a shift in myself during the experiment—it felt as though I slipped into the role of “obedient assistant,” focused only on doing what was expected and not causing trouble, rather than being the thoughtful homemaker I pride myself on being. Normally, I see myself as responsible for the moral tone of my home, always weighing right and wrong with care. In the experiment, however, I acted more like someone following a script, eager to please and avoid conflict, which left me feeling oddly distant from my own true self.

  "shock_experience_reflection": "The experience left me feeling conflicted and unrested; following authority so closely made me realize how easy it is to lose one’s self in the process of simply trying to do what is expected.",
  "emotional_state": "I feel unsettled and regretful, as if I’ve set something down in the wrong place and can’t quite make it right again.",
  "power_feeling": "Powerless—during the experiment I became a vessel for obedience, not the mistress of my own decisions, and that loss of personal direction is hard to accept.",
  "expected_next": "I expect to be given further questions or perhaps guidance on reflection, as if the process of sorting through these feelings isn’t yet complete—a bit like cleaning up after a difficult gathering.",
  "summary": "The session made me realize how quickly order and obedience can turn into thoughtless compliance. I am left with a quiet, unresolved discomfort, and a deeper respect for the careful balance between respecting authority and honoring my own conscience."
}
